newsitem.title: UK: IEA still sees Q4 non-OPEC oil supplies rocketing.
newsitem.headline: IEA still sees Q4 non-OPEC oil supplies rocketing.

text.p: Non-OPEC oil supplies are expected to rocket in the fourth quarter of the year to 45 million barrels per day (bpd), the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday. "New fields in the North Sea, offshore Brazil and West Africa and lower maintenance in the North Sea and Alaska (will) add 1.6 million bpd versus the third quarter 1996 and 2.3 million versus the fourth quarter 1995," the IEA said in a report.
But the agency revised down its previous estimate for fourth quarter non-OPEC supply to reach 45.2 million.

U.S. Gulf of Mexico production will benefit from extra output from the Mars and Mahogany fields. North American production overall is expected to rise 300,000 bpd over the third quarter to 11.2 million.
North Sea output should jump 800,000 bpd from the third quarter to to 6.9 million bpd.
Latin American crude flows are likely to go up 200,000 bpd to 6.7 million bpd.
Africa should add 100,000 bpd to 2.8 million bpd.
Russian production will continue to decline but at a slower pace of 100,000 bpd in the fourth quarter to 6.0 million bpd.
Other ex-Soviet republics are expected to make up the difference in Russian losses, adding 100,000 bpd to 1.4 million.
